sources.claim: Raw street-network geometry for the real town of Seaside, Florida (vertices, edges, segment lengths), and this case's own derived graph statistics: degree distribution, minimum-weight odd-vertex matchings (Chinese-postman / T-join solutions), and the Persimmon Connector candidate search
sources.value: 58 vertices; 86 edges; 3.9597 mi total (base network); 48 odd-degree vertices; 0.9046 mi minimum repeat mileage; deadhead ratio 1.2285. With the Persimmon Connector (I16-I54, 302 ft): 4.0169 mi total; 46 odd-degree vertices; 0.8236 mi minimum repeat mileage; deadhead ratio 1.2050.
sources.as_of: OSM data as of 2026-08-13 fetch; underlying street geometry is a live, editable dataset
sources.title: Seaside, Florida street-network data, retrieved via the Overpass API
sources.note: Raw way/node data fetched directly for the administrative-boundary bounding box of Seaside, FL (per Nominatim). This case's own pipeline: (1) collapsed raw OSM way geometry into a vertex/edge graph -- a vertex is any node shared by 2+ differently-named streets or a true dead end, an edge is the summed haversine-distance length of an uninterrupted same-named run between two such vertices; (2) excluded 3 way segments exceeding 0.2 mi that run into neighboring unmapped communities (treated as outside Renata's route district, SEE Appendix E MA2) and one disconnected 2-node fragment; (3) computed vertex degree directly by counting incident edges; (4) computed the minimum-weight matching of all odd-degree vertices (a T-join / route-inspection solution) using networkx's implementation of Galil's blossom algorithm over all-pairs shortest-path distances (Dijkstra) -- this is an exact optimum, not a heuristic; (5) searched all non-adjacent odd-vertex pairs within ~0.15 mi straight-line distance for the best Persimmon Connector candidate by resulting deadhead-ratio improvement. Full script logic and intermediate outputs are recorded in RESEARCH_LOG.md. Data (c) OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL 1.0 (https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright).

deliverables.text: A vertex-degree table for every vertex in the Larkspur Hollow Practice Block (a real 23-vertex excerpt of the full network), each vertex labeled EVEN or ODD.
A written Euler-circuit determination for the full network: which of the three possible cases applies, justified by the specific odd-degree vertex count given in Appendix B.

A minimum repeat-mileage route for the Practice Block: shortest-path pairing of every odd-degree vertex using the provided distance table, with the resulting deadhead ratio computed and compared to the full network's official ratio.

A capital-cost-versus-savings comparison for The Persimmon Connector on the full network: recomputed vertex degrees, reapplied Euler test, repeat mileage removed, cost vs. fuel savings, payback period.

appendices.title: Vertex Degree Table and Euler Determination
Larkspur Hollow Practice Block, and the Official As-Is Loop Numbers
The Persimmon Connector: Cost and Savings Data

balance.argument_a: No capital request, no construction risk, and the numbers are fully known today: a deadhead ratio of 1.2285, a fixed and predictable extra 0.9046 miles of repeat driving every sweep. On the only lens that has a real dollar figure attached -- fuel cost -- The Persimmon Connector is not close: at these sourced rates its payback period is on the order of millions of years, nowhere near the 20-40-year horizon any real capital budget uses.
balance.argument_b: The connector is a genuine, measurable improvement on the case's own stated primary metric: deadhead ratio drops from 1.2285 to 1.2050, a real 1.9% improvement, in the same family as this project's own gold-standard close-margin case (SPEC §2). It also permanently removes two odd-degree vertices from the network -- a structural fix, not a one-time workaround -- so every future sweep, indefinitely, benefits from it, not just this year's.
balance.margin_basis: Compare The As-Is Loop's official deadhead ratio (Appendix C, Part 2: 1.2285) against the deadhead ratio after The Persimmon Connector is built (Appendix D: 1.2050), both computed the same way (total miles driven / total miles serviced) over the same full 58-vertex network. margin_pct = (1.2285-1.2050)/1.2285 = 1.9%.

cohort_bands.note: Split the room into two desks -- one builds D1-D3 (The As-Is Loop, using the Practice Block) fully before seeing D4, the other jumps straight to modeling The Persimmon Connector on the full network -- then trade findings before the Data Deep Dive so both groups reconcile the same deadhead-ratio numbers and confront Appendix D's dollar-vs-ratio discrepancy together.
Work D1's Practice Block vertex-degree table together on the board as a warm-up, then split into pairs for D3 (Practice Block pairing) vs D4 (full-network connector) rather than four separate desks.

No vote at Anchor 1 -- the learner states an initial position (As-Is or Connector), and the guide argues the other side directly. Spend the recovered time on D3's odd-vertex pairing using the provided distance table, the step most likely to trip up a solo learner.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: The Larkspur Hollow street network's identity
modeling_assumptions.value_used: Modeled using the real, public street layout of the town of Seaside, Florida (OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL license) as a structural stand-in for the fictional city of Talbrook's Larkspur Hollow neighborhood
modeling_assumptions.basis: Talbrook is fictional, so no real street-network data exists for it. Seaside is a real, small, densely-platted town with a real, irregular, non-grid street layout -- exactly the kind of authentic vertex-degree irregularity a hand-drawn or invented grid could not honestly provide -- and its full network is public and directly downloadable via the Overpass API.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: The entire case -- the 48 odd-degree count, the deadhead ratio, the connector's effect -- depends on this specific real network's actual topology. A different real neighborhood would give different numbers and could change which vertices are the best connector candidates, though the qualitative finding (most real street networks have many odd-degree vertices, and a single new connector helps only marginally on a dollar basis) reflects a general graph-theory and municipal-economics pattern, not an artifact of this one network.

modeling_assumptions.value_used: Three OSM way segments exceeding 0.2 miles that extend beyond Seaside's built area toward neighboring, separately-mapped communities were excluded from the graph, along with one small disconnected 2-node fragment
modeling_assumptions.basis: OpenStreetMap draws some streets (East County Highway 30A, Forest Street, West Grove Avenue) as single continuous ways that run well past any sensible neighborhood boundary -- one segment ran 1.44 miles to a point far outside Seaside. Including their full real length would extend Renata's 'neighborhood' route over a mile into unrelated communities the case's own Background does not describe. The excluded segments are real pavement, just outside Larkspur Hollow's assigned route district -- the same way any real route supervisor's district has a boundary drawn somewhere.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Vertices where an excluded segment used to continue are treated as this district's own edge, not literal physical dead ends -- the street continues in reality, just outside Renata's assignment. This does not change the odd/even parity of any vertex that remains in-district; it only removes mileage and dead-end status that were never really Renata's to route.

modeling_assumptions.basis: Talbrook is fictional and has no real published sweeping schedule. The City of Austin, Texas's Resource Recovery Department publicly states residential streets are swept 'up to six times a year' (SEE Appendix F, S4) -- a real US municipal program's stated maximum, adopted here as Larkspur Hollow's assumed annual frequency.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Sweep frequency is a linear multiplier on every dollar figure in Appendix D -- halving it to 3/year would halve the (already astronomical) annual savings and double the payback period. It does not change the deadhead ratio itself, which is a per-sweep, frequency-independent quantity, so it has zero effect on the case's stated primary-metric margin (1.9%).

sensitivity_note: This case involves no illness, death, money stress, or family-hardship subject matter beyond an ordinary municipal budget memo; SPEC §6 does not require a facilitator flag beyond ordinary care with a case that touches a real household's tax dollars.
